items.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022
items.q: And George Plimpton, we were talking about it on Merv’s show.

ctx.x: Only ten minutes, and I would put cue cards on the floor to look down if I couldn’t think of what to talk about.

Well I’m going to tell you a perfect analogy of that. For some reason I’ve done a couple of shows with George Plimpton, the author. And you know George Plimpton, before he writes he does it. He played football with the Chicago Bears and he got busted up bad. Then he did a trapeze thing and threw his back out, but he does everything before he writes it. And George came to Vegas to do a comedy routine at Ceasar’s Palace, and he worked with Milton Berle and Alan King and Cosby. They said to him, “Do this: Light a…

is and when I broke my collar bone” he said, “none of those things came close to the pain that I suffered those eight minutes on stage with the entire audience looking at me and they hated me.” He said, “It’s a — it really is the worst death I’ve ever suffered in my life.”
